edition.locus: Cat. Lc. fr. 153 (Rauer), on Luke 16:1: incipit and explicit only

source_text: Ἐπεὶ δὲ ἀρετὴν εἶναι τὴν φρόνησιν expl. οὐρανοὺς ἡτοίμασεν ὁ κύριος.
pass_a_gloss: But since prudence (phronesis) [is] to be a virtue ... [explicit:] the Lord prepared heavens.
pass_b_english: But since prudence is a virtue … the Lord prepared the heavens (Proverbs 3:19).

lemmas.gloss: edition's mark: here ends (the omitted middle)

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 round 2: Pass B was a September summary about 'seek and save the lost' (Luke 19:10), which is not in this source; the published English had workroom marks '[break]' and '[fragmentary]'. Now the two printed phrases are translated, joined by an ellipsis for the edition's 'expl.'.
The edition's note (k*, Παροιμιῶν) shows the scholion comes from Origen on Proverbs; the full text is not in this source and is not supplied.

bible_refs.why: LXX: by prudence he prepared the heavens
